text: In some sub-Saharan African cities, more than 60% of urban residents live in informal settlements or slums — far higher than in wealthier regions where slums are a much smaller fraction of city populations
Inadequate housing is heavily concentrated in low-income countries — rapid urban growth has outpaced housing construction in cities across Africa, South Asia, and Latin America

In Nigeria alone, an estimated 40–50 million people live in substandard housing or informal settlements — a single country that illustrates how large the housing deficit is in rapidly urbanising Africa

Global homelessness has worsened since 2000 — the number of people without adequate shelter has grown substantially, driven by rapid urbanisation outpacing housing construction, conflict displacement, and climate-related housing loss.
India has an official houseless population of 1.77 million people, though civil rights groups estimate the actual number is closer to 3 million.
Slum Populations: Alongside street homelessness, an estimated 65 million people reside in precarious urban slums
Roughly 53% of India's homeless population lives in urban cities, driven by work migration and lack of affordable housing.
